chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who pierced a house, but was seized before he could reach anything. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He would be punished. So if he was seized and he had extracted goods, then upon him is the cutting (of the hand).'

He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him about a man who was seized and he was carrying a bundle of clothes, and he said that the owner of the house had given them to him.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The cutting would be staved off from him except if proof is established upon him. So if the proof is established upon him, he is cut.'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'The hand and the leg are cut, then no other (parts) are cut afterwards, but if he repeats, he is imprisoned and is maintained from the treasury of the Muslims.'

key_terms.الْقَطْعُ: Cutting (of the hand as a legal penalty)
key_terms.الْيَدُ وَ الرِّجْلُ: The hand and the leg (standard hadd limbs)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for cutting the hand in theft according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the jurisprudential nuances of hadd al-sariqah, emphasizing the critical distinction between mere entry and actual extraction of goods for determining the severity of punishment. It highlights the Shia legal principle of 'idrāʾ' (deferral of punishment) in cases of doubt regarding ownership, while clarifying that post-amputation recidivism results in imprisonment rather than repeated cutting. This reflects the broader Shia emphasis on precision in applying fixed penalties to ensure justice and mercy.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who pierced a hole in a house (to steal), but he was seized before he could arrive to anything. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would be punished. So if he was seized and he had extracted goods (from the house), so upon him would be the cutting (of the hand)’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who was seized and he was carrying a bundle of clothes, and said that the owner of the house had given these to him’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The cutting would be staved off from him except if the proof is established upon him. So if the proof is established upon him, his (hand) would be cut’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The hand and the leg would be cut, then no other (parts) of his be cut afterwards, but if he were to repeat, he would be imprisoned and would be expended upon from the public treasury of the Muslims’.
